aboutH2: Into Action Recovery Bear Creek: Men's Residential Recovery in Surrey
intro: Into Action Recovery Bear Creek is a men-only recovery house on 87B Avenue in Newton, a residential part of Surrey in Metro Vancouver. Men live there for the First Stage of Into Action's program, which the centre sets at 60 days or more, and spend the day in groups, one-to-one counselling and 12-step work.

It is the Into Action house with the longest provincial registration on file, and the one with the most Google reviews of its Surrey homes. The setting is a large family home with a fireplace, a formal dining room and a kitchen island, run by staff who mostly came through recovery themselves.

pillars.title: A Newton Family Home With Room to Sit Down Together
pillars.body: Bear Creek is a stucco house on a quiet Newton street, a few minutes from Bear Creek Park. The main floor has a living room with a gas fireplace, a front sitting room under a tall arched window and a dining room where the whole house eats at one table. The kitchen has an island and a fridge stocked with snacks, and residents can label and keep their own food. Upstairs and down, men sleep in single or shared rooms.

pillars.title: Groups Every Day, Steps Every Week
pillars.body: Into Action runs both educational groups and process groups each day, and every resident attends. Counsellors use CBT and DBT skills, SMART Recovery tools and the Twelve Steps, and the program has a step coach on staff. Men also get one-to-one counselling and go out with staff to AA and NA meetings in Surrey. Before discharge, each man builds an aftercare plan with his counsellor.

pillars.title: A Second Stage House if You Want One
pillars.body: Finishing First Stage does not have to mean going straight home. Into Action offers an optional Second Stage in sober living for 30 days or longer, with a curfew, daily chores, support meetings and counselling once a week on site. Men there go back to work or school while they keep the routine they built at Bear Creek. Recovery.com also lists mentoring and peer support as part of aftercare.

overviewH2: Into Action Recovery Bear Creek: Centre Overview
overview: Bear Creek takes adult men whose drinking or drug use has stopped being manageable at home, including men who have relapsed after earlier treatment. It is a non-medical residence registered with the province, so withdrawal has to be finished before admission, and mental health care stays with each man's own doctor or the virtual clinic Into Action works with.

location.heading: Into Action Recovery Bear Creek in Surrey, British Columbia
location.intro: The Bear Creek house is on 87B Avenue in Newton, one of Surrey's largest residential areas, a short drive west of Bear Creek Park and King George Boulevard. Downtown Vancouver is about 40 minutes away by car over the Alex Fraser or Pattullo bridges, Burnaby about 30 minutes, Langley and White Rock around 20 minutes, and Abbotsford in the Fraser Valley roughly 40 minutes along Highway 1.

faqIntro: Answers come from Into Action's own website, BC's Assisted Living Registry and public listings. Still unsure? Call, it's free and confidential.

faqs.q: How much does Into Action Recovery Bear Creek cost?
faqs.a: recovery.com estimates $10,000 to $30,000 CAD for a stay at Bear Creek, depending on how long you stay. Into Action is private pay and does not publish a fee table, so admissions gives the full cost on your first call. The centre says it can help families look at payment options.

faqs.q: How long is the program at Bear Creek?
faqs.a: Into Action calls its First Stage residential program a 60-day minimum, with extensions when they help. Its other pages also mention 30, 60 and 90-day stays, and recovery.com lists 30 to 90 days. The length is set at intake and reviewed while you are there.

faqs.q: Is Bear Creek a medical treatment centre?
faqs.a: No. Bear Creek is a supportive recovery residence. Into Action says it has no doctors or nurses on site and works with virtual healthcare providers, or your own doctor, for medication and medical care.

faqs.q: Does Into Action Recovery Bear Creek offer detox?
faqs.a: No. Men who need medically supervised withdrawal have to finish detox at another facility before admission. Into Action's admissions team says it can help line up detox so there is no gap before you move in.

faqs.q: Where is Bear Creek and how do I get there?
faqs.a: The house is at 13222 87B Avenue in Newton, Surrey, a short drive from Bear Creek Park and King George Boulevard. Downtown Vancouver is about 40 minutes away by car, and Langley and White Rock are each around 20 minutes. Admissions arranges your arrival date and can help with travel from outside the Lower Mainland.

faqs.q: Who can stay at Bear Creek?
faqs.a: Adult men with alcohol or drug problems. Into Action has been men-only since 2012. It treats alcohol, opioids including fentanyl and heroin, cocaine and crack, benzodiazepines, prescription drugs, cannabis and MDMA, and many residents use more than one substance.

faqs.q: Is Bear Creek licensed in British Columbia?
faqs.a: Yes. BC's Assisted Living Registry lists Into Action - Bear Creek at 13222 87B Avenue as a registered supportive recovery residence, registration SU2016-000006, in the Fraser Health region.

faqs.q: Can I leave the house or have visitors during my stay?
faqs.a: Yes, after an initial restriction period. Staff take residents to community meetings, shopping, walks and hikes from the start. Once restrictions lift you can ask for personal outings and weekend passes, and family contact can begin to the degree you want it.

Men who finish First Stage can move into Into Action's Second Stage sober living for 30 days or longer. It keeps curfew, chores, support meetings and weekly on-site counselling while you go back to work or school. It is optional.

faqs.q: Can I smoke at Bear Creek?
faqs.a: Yes, in designated areas only. That is Into Action's policy across its houses, and recovery.com lists the same rule for Bear Creek.
